info.name: VisorShield — Universal AI Governance Proxy
info.description:
Sample client: **Metro Pacific BPO Solutions Inc.**, a Philippine BPO with four lines of business, each mapped to a VisorShield industry profile:

- **govtech** — LGU citizen hotline (Barangay/city hall transactions, PH_TIN/PH_SSS/PH_PHILSYS)
- **healthcare** — after-hours nurse triage line for a US clinic client (HIPAA)
- **fintech** — bank collections/customer support line (PCI-DSS)
- **legal_hr** — internal HR shared-services helpdesk for Metro Pacific's own employees

## Auth
VisorShield has no `/login` endpoint — JWTs are minted out-of-band and validated with `JWT_SECRET` (HS256). This collection's **collection-level Pre-request Script** mints short-lived `app` / `admin` / `compliance_officer` tokens on every request using CryptoJS (bundled in the Postman sandbox), signed with the `jwt_secret` collection variable.

**Before running:** set `jwt_secret` to match your server's `JWT_SECRET` env var (defaults to `change-me-in-production` in `app/config.py` for local dev — already set below). Set `base_url` to your running instance (default `http://localhost:8000`).

## Flow
1. Run **Admin → Create Organization** first — it captures the new `org_id` into `org_id_created` and chains into the rest of the Admin folder.
2. Proxy/Extension requests use `org_id` (a fixed seeded org) by default — swap to `org_id_created` if you want to exercise a freshly created org end-to-end.

exec: // Mints fresh HS256 JWTs for the app/admin/compliance_officer roles on
// every request, since VisorShield has no /login endpoint — tokens are
// issued out-of-band and only need to satisfy app/middleware/auth.py.
// Uses CryptoJS, which ships in the Postman sandbox.
// industry_type is minted PER REQUEST from that request's own
// X-Industry-Type header (defaulting to 'govtech' for requests that
// don't set one, e.g. Admin/Audit calls) because auth.py rejects any
// token whose industry_type claim doesn't exactly match the header —
// see CLAUDE.md 'JWT Claims Schema'. A single fixed claim value can't
// This request's own X-Industry-Type header, if it sets one.

request.description: Liveness/readiness probe. Checks Postgres, Redis, Presidio and the embedding model. Returns 503 if any dependency is down.

Unauthenticated, like /health — scope access at the network layer. Exposes visorshield_requests_total, visorshield_requests_blocked_total, visorshield_guardrail_incidents_total and visorshield_pipeline_step_duration_ms in Prometheus exposition format.
PII in the prompt (PERSON, PH_TIN, PH_SSS, PHONE_NUMBER) should be masked by the govtech profile before it reaches the LLM. Check the `X-VisorShield-PII-Masked` response header.

item.name: Healthcare — Nurse Triage Line (US clinic client)

request.description: PERSON, DATE_TIME, PHONE_NUMBER and EMAIL_ADDRESS should be masked under the HIPAA/DPA (healthcare) profile.
PCI-DSS/SEC profile — expects CREDIT_CARD and PH_TIN to be masked. Card number used is the well-known Visa test PAN (4111 1111 1111 1111), not a real card.
Bias/sensitivity profile — expects PERSON, AGE, EMAIL_ADDRESS and PHONE_NUMBER to be masked.
By default the full response is buffered and PII-scanned before anything streams to the client (step 5 runs before any byte is sent), unless the org's JWT sets `allow_streaming_passthrough: true`.
Expected: HTTP 451. Hits the govtech keyword blocklist ("vote for", "campaign material") at the guardrails layer — never forwarded to the LLM.
Expected: HTTP 403 model_not_permitted. `gpt-4-turbo` is not in the token's `allowed_models` list minted by the collection's pre-request script.
Expected: HTTP 422 invalid_industry_type. Fail-closed check — an unrecognized/missing profile is rejected before any pipeline step runs.
Expected: HTTP 401 missing_or_invalid_token.
Simulates the browser extension capturing a chatgpt.com composer prompt before it's sent. Response includes masked_prompt, per-entity map, risk_level and prior_flags_this_month.
Step 5 for the extension surface — audits PII the model introduced into its answer. Returns entity types + placeholders only, never original values.
Device-side enforcement policy the extension caches (~10 min) for the calling org.
Metadata-only telemetry sink — the model rejects any event carrying prompt text (extra="forbid").
Liveness ping so the compliance dashboard can show which agent workstations are actively protected.
compliance_officer is locked to their own org (from the JWT); admin may pass ?org_id for any org or omit it for all orgs.
404 (not 403) is returned when the transaction is out of the caller's org scope, so record existence isn't leaked cross-tenant.
Aggregate totals for the caller's org: requests, tokens, cost, PII events prevented, guardrail hits, compliance rate.

"Who is using AI, how much" rollup — cost/tokens/request count grouped by the X-VisorShield-User identity resolved on each transaction. Previously unanswerable: every caller behind a shared API key looked identical.
Bulk download (capped at 50,000 rows/call — page with date_from for more) including the hash-chain fields (chain_seq/prev_hash/record_hash) so the export can be independently re-verified offline.

Recomputes the per-org SHA-256 hash chain over transactions + guardrail_incidents and reports the first broken link, if any. What makes "immutable audit" a checkable claim rather than a policy statement.
Onboards Metro Pacific BPO Solutions Inc. under the govtech profile for its Citizen Hotline line of business.
Raises the monthly budget after Metro Pacific added a second BPO seat cluster for the Citizen Hotline. Partial update — only provided fields change.
The raw key is returned once and never shown again — store it securely. It is NOT the same thing as the collection's self-signed JWTs, which authenticate against JWT_SECRET directly.
Revokes a specific key, e.g. after a workstation is decommissioned. Swap {{key_id_to_revoke}} for {{api_key_id_created}} to revoke the key created above.
Org-specific embedding overrides for the Layer 3 (semantic) guardrail check, on top of the default govtech keyword blocklist and Layer 2 prompt-injection heuristics.
Reverts the org to the default in-process govtech embeddings for Layer 3 guardrails.
Org-scoped grouping an admin curates — not auto-discovered like AI Inventory. department_id is a single FK on users (see Identity Model in CLAUDE.md).
Unlike departments, groups are cross-cutting — a user can belong to several via user_group_memberships.

Queries the seeded {{org_id}} (not {{org_id_created}}) by default, since that's the org the Proxy/Extension folders actually send X-VisorShield-User traffic against — users are auto-provisioned, never hand-created, so this list is empty until some traffic runs.
Run List Users first to populate {{user_id}} — users are only ever auto-provisioned from X-VisorShield-User, this endpoint just curates the resulting row.

Groups are cross-cutting (many-to-many). Run Create Group and List Users first so {{group_id}}/{{user_id}} are populated — note the demo group lives under {{org_id_created}} while the demo user lives under {{org_id}}; swap in matching IDs from your own environment for a realistic run.
Auto-discovered from every completed transaction's (provider, model_used) — not hand-entered. Global, not org-scoped.
Governance flag only — not a pricing or access-control source. Run List AI Inventory — Models first to populate {{model_id}}.
Auto-discovered from every transaction's app_source — the shadow-AI surface. Queries {{org_id}} since that's the org the Proxy/Extension folders actually generate app_source traffic for.
Toggle sanctioned status for a calling application. Run List AI Inventory — Apps first to populate {{app_id}}.
One row per device_id, upserted by POST /v1/extension/heartbeat — run Browser Extension → Device Heartbeat first to see {{device_id}} appear here.
Soft-deletes the org (is_active=false) and revokes every one of its API keys. Run this last if you're cleaning up after exercising the collection end-to-end.
